subject.title: Browser tool needs a CDP/IME text insertion action for contenteditable editors like X composer

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser act action for native/CDP text insertion, and what exact contract should it expose for managed CDP versus existing-session profiles?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the action name, focus/target semantics, driver support, unsupported behavior, and safety proof are public browser-tool API decisions that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Add native insert action
options.body: Define a new browser act kind that uses CDP Input.insertText for managed/remote CDP profiles and returns explicit unsupported errors for drivers that cannot provide native insertion.

options.title: Keep using type/fill
options.body: Decline a new action and document that rich-editor IME failures require site-specific workarounds or external automation until a broader browser-input design exists.

options.title: Defer to plugin API design
options.body: Pause this issue until maintainers decide whether browser input extension points should move into a plugin/SDK seam rather than expanding the bundled browser action contract.

recommendation.title: Add native insert action
recommendation.body: Define a new browser act kind that uses CDP Input.insertText for managed/remote CDP profiles and returns explicit unsupported errors for drivers that cannot provide native insertion.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger appears in the browser plugin runtime introduction history and is the strongest current owner signal available from git history.
